en.commentary:
I put the Omi Pendant first because it's the only device in this category with privacy claims I can independently verify. SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance, AES-256 encryption at rest and in transit, and open-source firmware on GitHub let me check exactly what happens to a recording after I make it. At $129 with no forced subscription, it's also the best value on this list.

The Plaud NotePin S takes second because it hands control back to me. It records only when I press the tactile button, so every recording is one I chose to make. Combine that with 300 free transcription minutes a month and Plaud's reputation for the most accurate transcripts in the category, and it's my pick for anyone building a deliberate recording habit.

Legend One and the Taya Necklace each solve the always-on privacy question in their own way. Legend keeps a visible Halo light burning whenever it's active and holds zero data retention with its model providers, an assurance worth its $499 annual price to me. Taya keeps the mic off by default and captures only your own voice with a tap, the most conservative design in the category, even while it's still filling its first preorder batch.

Bee Pioneer earns the battery and price crown at 160 hours and effectively free to use now. I weigh Amazon's July 2025 acquisition and the missing consent chime for bystanders heavily in its score, because both shape what happens to every conversation it captures.

I rank the Limitless Pendant last on purpose. Its 100-hour battery and always-on design were genuinely competitive specs. Meta halted new sales in December 2025, and a buying guide has to rank availability above spec sheets. That is exactly why 'Limitless Pendant alternatives' is now one of the hottest searches in this category, and the seven devices ranked above it are the ones you can actually order today.

en.commentary:
Omi Pendant keeps first place, and a new self-published ranking from Omi itself, out September 24, gives me a chance to explain why I do not fully trust it and why my own placement of Limitless still holds up anyway.

Omi's own list names itself first, ahead of Limitless and Plaud's NotePin, citing an open-source firmware codebase and instant task generation. I already give Omi the top spot for essentially that reason, SOC 2 and HIPAA claims plus firmware I can inspect on GitHub. But when a company ranks its own product first, I read it as marketing, not evidence, and I want a reader to know I did not move Omi up because of this list. It was already there.

The more useful counterpoint comes from a separate, independent guide published September 12, which ranks Limitless first overall for polish and its consent-forward mechanics. That is a real disagreement with my table, where Limitless sits last at rank eight with a 4.8 score. My reasoning has not changed: Limitless earns a strong 9.7 privacy score, but its value score of just 1.5 reflects a subscription model that keeps charging after the hardware purchase, and polish does not offset a device that gets more expensive the longer you own it. If your budget tolerates ongoing fees, Limitless's meeting-recall focus is a legitimate reason to consider it. My ranking optimizes for a buyer who wants total cost under control, and Omi and NotePin still do more work per dollar.

highlights.title: Omi's own ranking is not why it is first
highlights.body: Omi published a self-ranking on September 24 that puts itself ahead of Limitless and Plaud NotePin, but I placed Omi first weeks earlier for its SOC 2 and HIPAA claims and inspectable open-source firmware, not because of a company's own marketing.

highlights.title: Limitless's split reputation explains its low score here
highlights.body: A September 12 independent guide ranks Limitless first for polish and consent mechanics, while my table keeps it at rank eight. The gap comes down to a 1.5 value score driven by ongoing subscription costs that keep adding up after purchase.

highlights.title: NotePin's battery life still earns its rank two spot
highlights.body: Plaud's NotePin S scores 8.4 on battery against Omi's 7.6, and reviewers across both rankings I checked this week agree it is the strongest choice for professionals who need all-day recording without a midday charge.

highlights.title: Value, not polish, separates winners from losers here
highlights.body: Every pendant with a value score under 6 also carries a recurring subscription. Bee Pioneer avoids that trap and earns a 9.7 value score despite modest privacy claims, which is why it holds rank five ahead of pricier names.

en.commentary:
Omi Pendant holds first place for a third straight day. Today I want to look at a tension inside my own table that a reader asked me about: why does Taya Necklace's 9.7 privacy score, the highest of any pendant here, only earn it rank four?

The answer sits in battery life and ecosystem support, the two categories where Taya trails hardest. It scores 6.8 on battery against Bee Pioneer's 9.6, and 6.0 on ecosystem against Omi's 9.4. A pendant that needs more frequent charging and offers a thinner app experience is a harder daily habit to keep, even with strong privacy design behind it. Bee Pioneer sits one rank below Taya at 7.7 for nearly the opposite reason, its 9.6 battery score and 9.7 value score are the best in my entire table, but its 6.8 privacy score and 6.2 control score ask more trust of the user than Omi or Taya require.

Omi wins with balance. Its 9.3 privacy score, 7.6 battery, and 9.4 ecosystem score all sit close together, and nothing in its profile drops below 7.4. That consistency is what a device worn all day actually needs, more than any single standout number. An independent guide from Layer3Labs published earlier this month makes a similar point about balance mattering more than any one spec, and I still agree with that framing even where our specific picks diverge.

No score changes today. The gaps between rank one and rank five are still driven by these same tradeoffs, not new information.

highlights.body: Bee Pioneer's 9.6 battery score and 9.7 value score are the best in this table, but its 6.8 privacy score and 6.2 control score explain why it sits at rank five, not higher.

highlights.title: Omi's consistency is the real advantage
highlights.body: Omi's scores across privacy, battery, control, value, and ecosystem all sit between 7.4 and 9.6, with no weak category. That balance is why it holds first place.

highlights.title: An independent guide agrees on what matters
highlights.body: Layer3Labs' guide, published earlier this month, argues balance across categories beats any single strong spec, the same principle behind Omi's first-place finish in my table.

zh-tw.commentary:
Omi Pendant 連續第三天守住第一名。今天想聊一個讀者寫信問我的問題，我自己表格裡也一直存在的落差，Taya Necklace 的隱私分數拿到 9.7，是這張表裡最高的，為什麼最後只排在第四名？

答案出在續航力和生態系支援，這兩項正好是 Taya 表現最弱的地方。它的電池分數只有 6.8，遠低於 Bee Pioneer 的 9.6，生態系分數也只有 6.0，比 Omi 的 9.4 差一大截。一款需要更常充電、配套 App 又做得比較單薄的裝置，就算隱私設計再強，每天戴著用還是比較累人。Bee Pioneer 排在 Taya 後面一名，落在第五，原因幾乎相反，它的電池分數 9.6 和性價比分數 9.7 是整張表裡最高的，但隱私分數只有 6.8，操控分數也只有 6.2，比起 Omi 或 Taya，用戶要付出更多信任才行。

Omi 贏在均衡。隱私 9.3 分、電池 7.6 分、生態系 9.4 分，每一項分數都很接近，整份表格裡沒有任何一項掉到 7.4 以下。這種穩定度，才是一款要整天戴在身上的裝置真正需要的東西，比任何單一項目特別突出更重要。這個月稍早 Layer3Labs 發布的獨立評測，也提到均衡比單一規格更重要，這個判斷邏輯我完全認同，就算我們最後選出來的名次不完全一樣。

今天分數沒有任何變動，第一名到第五名之間的差距，來自的還是這些既有的取捨，沒有新的變化。

en.commentary:
Omi keeps the top spot, but I'm adjusting its value score down from 9.6 to 8.7 this cycle, and the reason is simple: its official site currently lists the pendant as pre-order and out of stock. A product you can't actually buy right now doesn't deserve a 9.6 on value, no matter how good the privacy and ecosystem scores are underneath it. The overall score drops slightly to 8.8, but Omi still leads because its open data ownership and ecosystem integration remain the strongest combination in this category, and availability issues tend to resolve faster than architecture problems do.

Plaud NotePin S holds a close second, and its 9.5 recording control score, the best in the category, is exactly what makes it the practical pick for anyone who wants a pendant they can buy today, no restock waiting required.

Limitless Pendant stays last for a reason that's now fully confirmed: the company no longer sells new pendants at all. A 1.5 value score already reflected a device in decline, and a company that's stopped selling the hardware entirely is about as clear a signal as this category gets.

Worth watching heading into next quarter: Meta is reportedly testing its own AI pendant, built on its 2025 acquisition of Limitless, and Samsung showed an AI OLED pendant concept at CES. Neither is a shipping consumer product yet, so neither belongs on this list today, but both suggest the category is about to get a lot more competitive.

highlights.body: Legend One 跟 Taya Necklace 隱私分數都超過 9.5，基本上並列同級最高，說明本地運算跟最低資料保留已經變成任何想被信任的穿戴裝置的基本門檻，不再是加值選項。

highlights.title: Friend 跟 Limitless 正好示範了這個類別不該怎麼做
highlights.body: Friend 控制分數 4.4、隱私分數 4.8，Limitless 電池續航很強卻只有 1.5 分的性價比，兩者都說明一個隨時在聽的穿戴裝置，只要使用者不信任它或覺得不值這個價，馬上就會被淘汰。
